OVERVIEW

[
1
]

Dr. Andrew Feifer (“Dr. Feifer”) and Jonathan
Feifer (“Mr. Feifer”) seek the issuance of an interlocutory injunction against Glenn
J. Feldman (“Mr. Feldman”) whom they allege has made and disseminated false,
libelous and vexatious statements about them with the intention to discredit
them and to lead others to believe they are thieves and war criminals.

[
2
]

Mr. Feldman contests.

do the plaintiffs have a right to an interlocutory injunction?

1.1

Facts relevant to the issue

[
3
]

Dr. Feifer is a urologist specialized in
urologic oncology surgeries. He lives in Ontario.

[
4
]

Mr. Feifer is the managing partner of an
investment company. He lives in New-York.

[
5
]

Both individuals are members of the Jewish
community.

[
6
]

Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer are the liquidators to
the Estate of their late mother Sherry Lande Feifer (“Sherry”).

[
7
]

Sherry was the sister of Irwin Lande (“Irwin”).

[
8
]

Sherry and Irwin were the children of Martin
Lande (“Martin”) and Mia Lande (“Mia”).

[
9
]

Martin died in 1996, leaving most of his Estate
to his wife Mia.

[
10
]

Mia died in November 2015 and left her assets,
including those of her late husband Martin, to her children Sherry and Irwin
and her grandchildren.

[
11
]

In August 2016, Sherry died, leaving her
inheritance to her two sons, Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer.

[
12
]

Mr. Feldman is a lawyer and member of the Bar of
Québec as well as a businessman primarily active in the real estate industry.

[
13
]

Mr. Feldman and Irwin were friends and business
partners for many years, prior to the breakdown of their personal and business relationship.

[
14
]

In particular, Mr. Feldman and Irwin were partners
and shareholders with others in Société en commandite Montréal Media &
Divertissement and Montréal Media Entertainment Building Inc. (the
“Businesses”).

[
15
]

The Estate of Sherry is also a shareholder in
the Businesses, such that Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer are involved in the
Businesses as well, in their capacity as heirs to the Estate of Sherry.

[
16
]

In 2019, Mr. Feldman began accusing Irwin,
amongst other things, of being in possession of millions (which eventually became
allegations of billions) of USD in gold bars stolen from Holocaust victims by
the Nazis (the “Allegations”).

[
17
]

Mr. Feldman contends that a cousin of the Lande
family, Dr. Ludwig Delphiner, “was a Waffen-S.S. officer with Adolf Hitler’s
German Third Reich regime, and was in charge of inventory for gold, art and
jewellery from the Jewish Holocaust victims at the Auschwitz death camp in Nazi
occupied Poland during the Second World War”.
[1]

[
18
]

According to Mr. Feldman, Dr. Delphiner
immigrated to Canada with or subsequently repatriated billions of dollars in gold
bars from the Auschwitz concentration camp in Poland and held these gold bars
in his residence located in Ïle Bizard, Quebec.
[2]

[
19
]

Mr. Feldman further asserts that Irwin and his
father Martin, forged Dr. Delphiner’s will in the 80’s in order for Martin to
solely inherit Dr. Delphiner’s gold bars.
[3]

[
20
]

The gold bars were then inherited by Mia, who
left her fortune to Sherry and Irwin, thus the Allegations.

[
21
]

Mr. Feldman shared his Allegations with his
other partners in the Businesses, which led to the signing of an extraordinary
resolution in which property rights as well as Irwin’s signing authority in the
Businesses were suspended (the “Resolution”).
[4]

[
22
]

The Resolution also extends to units held by Dr.
Feifer and Mr. Feifer as heirs to the different Lande estates.

[
23
]

In light of the existing conflict between Mr.
Feldman and himself, Irwin commenced commercial proceedings on March 23, 2020
requesting the appointment of a receiver/sequestrator for the Businesses (the
“Commercial Proceedings”).

[
24
]

On March 27, 2020 representations were made by
the parties to the Commercial Proceedings and Justice Marie-Anne Paquette
granted Irwin’s request to appoint a receiver for the Businesses.
[5]

[
25
]

In her judgment, Justice Paquette indicates that
the serious feud between Irwin and Dr. Fiefer, on the one hand, and Mr. Feldman
and other shareholders on the other hand, makes it impossible for them to
continue to operate the Businesses smoothly.
[6]

[
26
]

Other judgments were subsequently rendered in
the context of the Commercial Proceedings reporting the evident hostility of
Mr. Feldman towards Irwin and others.
[7]

[
27
]

After the hearing on March 27, 2020 and in light
of what he perceived as Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer siding with Irwin, Mr.
Feldman continued to disseminate his Allegations, now implicating Dr. Feifer and
Mr. Feifer.

[
28
]

More specifically, on March 31, 2020, Mr.
Feldmand sent a detailed affidavit (the “Long Form Affidavit”)
[8]
to Justice Paquette, after she
rendered her decision in the Commercial Proceedings, in which he explains at
length his alleged discoveries regarding Irwin’s possession of 2.6 billion in USD
gold bars stolen from Holocaust victims by the Nazis.

[
29
]

In the Long Form Affidavit, Mr. Feldman further
states that:

29.1.

“(…) as well as to the exclusion of Irwin’s (J.J. and Andrew Feifer)
nephewswhom we belive were equally living off proceeds of Dr. Delphiner’s
Estate through the inheritance of their mother Sherri Feifer”;
[9]

29.2.

“(…) none of the properties, which Irwin and/or his nephews are
involved with me and my co-partners, rightfully belong to him or to them, they
rather belong to the survivors of the holocaust (…)”;
[10]

29.3.

“(…) the only reason for the Feifer sons to have taken the side of
their Uncle, Irwin Lande, was to defend and protect their similar gold
Inheritances from the origination of Dr. Ludwig Delphiner or Delfiner…”.
[11]

[
30
]

Similar direct and indirect accusations are also
expressed by Mr. Feldman in different disturbing videos recorded by him (the
“Videos”).
[12]

[
31
]

The Long Form Affidavit and Videos were
communicated to different third parties
[13]

by Mr. Feldman with the intent to reveal what he believes is the truth.

[
32
]

In this regard, Mr. Feldman specifically says in
one of the Videos that once he discovered the Allegations, he “went on a
mission to get to the bottom of this”.
[14]

[
33
]

On April 8, 2020, after having been informed of
the Long Form Affidavit, Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer summoned Mr. Feldman to
cease and desist from defamatory remarks concerning them.
[15]

[
34
]

On April 20, 2020, Mr. Feldman’s lawyer
responded :

It should be clear that your clients were never
targeted by Me Feldman’s legal declaration in this matter until your clients,
of their on volition, decided to team up with their uncle Irwin Lande (…) This
juggle of positions by your clients made it clear to many of the partners that
your clients were actually siding up with Mr. Lande’s legal posture for the
sole purpose of protecting their own pot of gold and/or inheritances from the
Estate of Mia Lande and/or Sherry Feifer.

(…)

Our client has no alternative should your clients not
wish to cooperate and any futher conversations with authorities will
necessarily include your clients as direct and willing participants in this
alleged massive heist of wealth, traceable to the origins of death camps in
Nazi occupied Poland and Germany, which history neither you or your clients can
whitewash with newspaper clippings fabricated by the “doc” himself.
[16]

[
35
]

Additional exchanges occurred between the
parties in connection with the Allegations
[17]

over the course of the following months.

[
36
]

Ultimately, on July 10, 2020, Dr. Feifer and Mr.
Feifer filed their Originating Application for the issuance of an interlocutory
and permanent injunction (the “Demand”).

[
37
]

On November 5, 2020, in support of his
contestation of the Demand, Mr. Feldman filed a
de bene esse
defense and
crossclaim (the “Defense”) as well as exhibits D-1 to D- 3.

[
38
]

In his Defense, Mr. Feldman pleads his
statements are accurate and Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer are aware that the
funds they inherited from their mother’s Estate were derived in whole or in
part, from illicit activities.
[18]

[
39
]

The Defense also contains a number of judicial
admissions.

[
40
]

More specifically, at paragraph 22 of his
Defense, Mr. Feldman admits the allegations contained in paragraphs 5, 7, 8,
14, 15, 16, 21, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 32, 36, 38, 39, 51, 55, 56, 67,
69 and 76 of the Demand.

[
41
]

Paragraph 38 of the Demand read as follow:

38. Feldman’s fictitious and grossly defamatory statements
demonstrate that there are no limits to his pursuit of creating a fictitious
narrative to accommodate his position, particularly so as the Plaintiffs and
Sherry are in fact the descendants of Holocaust survivors, with many family
members having perished in concentration camps.

[
42
]

On November 11 and 16, 2020, Mr. Feldman was
examined out of court on his Defense
[19]
.

[
43
]

In his lengthy pre-trial examination, Mr.
Feldman said :

(…) No one except your clients, for their own selfish
motives, their greedy motives, their piggish motives, and Lande, for the same
motives, another pig, another selfish, greedy, but... of course wanted to
liquidate the building, to punish me and my partners for invoking something
that was true.

(…)

An so, yes, I was extremely angry, frustrated. What
you did was you allowed… and your clients, who I will sue right after for all
these damages, they’re going to be sued for all the damages that MNP cost me,
cost my partners, and all the legal fees, they’ll be sued. That’s guaranteed.
They’ll be coming to Quebec quite often. And I like to make sure people come to
Quebec in January/February because the weather’s really nice at that time.
[20]

[
44
]

No other evidence has been filed to date by Mr.
Feldman in support of his contestation of the Demand.

1.2

Legal principles

[
45
]

Article 511
C.C.P.
provides that :

511. An interlocutory injunction may be granted if the
applicant appears to have a right to it and it is judged necessary to prevent
serious or irreparable prejudice to the applicant or to avoid creating a
factual or legal situation that would render the judgment on the merits
ineffective.

(…)

[
46
]

The conditions for the issuance of a prohibitive
interlocutory injunction are an appearance of right, serious or irreparable
harm and balance of inconvenients.
[21]

[
47
]

However, when a prohibitive interlocutory
injunction is sought in the context of a defamation case, the Court of Appeal
has specified :

57. D'entrée de jeu, il faut reconnaître que le test
traditionnel pour justifier le prononcé d'une ordonnance d'injonction
interlocutoire n'est pas celui qui est approprié si l'injonction recherchée
vise à interdire la diffusion des déclarations diffamatoires. Cela tient
essentiellement à l'utilisation inappropriée des critères du poids des
inconvénients et du préjudice irréparable qui, en matière de diffamation,
peuvent difficilement favoriser l'auteur des propos dits diffamatoires. Ce qui
a pour effet de restreindre sinon de scléroser la liberté d'expression. C'est
la conclusion à laquelle en est venue la Cour suprême dans l'affaire
Canadian
Liberty Net
.

58. Tel que rappelé plus haut dans
Canadian
Liberty Net
, la
Cour suprême citait avec approbation les critères retenus par notre Cour sous
la plume du juge Rothman dans l'arrêt
Champagne
. Il y a lieu d'y revenir.

59. Comme en l'espèce, l'arrêt
Champagne
traitait d'une injonction
interlocutoire prononcée dans l'attente de l'audition d'une action en
diffamation. L'ordonnance rendue par la Cour supérieure se lisait ainsi :

Ne pas diffamer, ridiculiser et calomnier de quelque façon que ce soit,
directement ou indirectement, la et à l'encontre de la partie demanderesse
requérante, ses officiers entre autres son directeur général, M. Jacques
Vézina, ses administrateurs, dirigeants et employés, en diffusant sur les ondes
des propos à caractère diffamatoire ou vexatoire entre autres, de la nature et
du genre de ceux soulignés dans le présent jugement ou incitant la population à
tenir de tels propos à l'égard de la partie demanderesse requérante, ses
officiers, entre autres et notamment son directeur général, M. Jacques Vézina,
ses administrateurs, dirigeants et employés.

60. Dans un premier temps, le juge Rothman rappelle
que la Cour supérieure a entièrement compétence pour prononcer une ordonnance
d'injonction interlocutoire afin d'interdire tous propos diffamatoires, et ce,
dans l'attente de l'audition au fond de l'action.

61. En deuxième lieu, souligne-t-il, cette compétence
sera exercée avec prudence. Elle sera réservée aux situations les plus claires
et rares où le caractère diffamant ou injurieux des propos est évident et ne
peut être justifié d'aucune façon. Encore là, l'ordonnance d'injonction ne sera
prononcée que si la preuve établit, de façon prépondérante, que l'auteur a
l'intention de récidiver.

62. Troisièmement, dans tous les cas l'ordonnance
recherchée doit viser des propos précis, et ce, pour deux motifs. D'abord,
l'ordonnance en termes généraux qui interdit de diffamer a pour effet de porter
indûment atteinte à la liberté d'expression et a nécessairement un effet de
bâillon (chilling effect) pour la personne visée.

63. Finalement, cela ne signifie pas que l'auteur de
la faute ne sera pas sanctionné pour ces propos diffamatoires ou injurieux. Il
le sera, le cas échéant, par l'octroi de dommages-intérêts à la suite de
l'audition au fond.
[22]

[
48
]

In
Champagne c.

Collège d'enseignement général et professionnel de
Jonquière
, Justice Robert summarised the applicable criteria for the
issuance of an interlocutory injunction in a defamation case as follows:

55 Brown propose certaines règles
pour émettre une telle injonction, tirées principalement des différents arrêts
rendus dont les plus importants sont cités par mon collègue Rothman. Je résume
ces règles de la façon suivante:

1. Le pouvoir discrétionnaire du juge d'émettre une telle injonction
doit être exercé avec une
très grande prudence
;

2. L'injonction ne peut être accordée que dans les situations les
plus
claires
et les
rares
.

3. Les paroles ou les écrits prohibés doivent être
clairement
diffamatoires
.

4. Le préjudice causé par les paroles ou les mots doit être
irréparable
.

5. L'appelant ne nie pas la véracité des propos ou s'il les nie,
sa
défense de justification est dépourvue de succès
.
[23]

[
49
]

In the 2016 edition of the
Dictionnaire de
droit québécois et canadien
, diffamation is defined as:

Allégation orale ou écrite qui porte
atteinte, involontairement ou de façon délibérée, à la réputation d'une
personne vivante ou décédée.
[24]

[
50
]

In criminal law, defamatory libel is defined as:

Acte criminel qui consiste à publier
ou à faire diffuser, sans raison valable, un écrit mensonger qui vise à
insulter une personne ou à nuire à sa réputation, que la personne diffusant
l'information sache ou ignore que l'écrit est faux.
[25]

[
51
]

In
Ville de Longueuil

c.

Théodore
,
Justice Stéphane Sansfaçon summarised the Suprême Court and the Court of Appeal’s
teachings on defamation as following:

7 Dans l'arrêt
Prud'homme
c
.
Prud'homme
la Cour suprême du Canada expose qu'il y
aura diffamation lorsqu'un citoyen ordinaire estimerait que les propos tenus,
pris dans leur ensemble, ont déconsidéré la réputation d'un tiers, soit par les
idées qu'elle exprime explicitement, soit par les insinuations qui s'en
dégagent.

8 Dans
Société Radio-Canada
c.
Radio Sept-Îles inc.
, la Cour d'appel du Québec enseigne que la
diffamation consiste en des propos ou des écrits qui font perdre l'estime ou la
considération de quelqu'un ou qui suscitent à son égard des sentiments
défavorables ou désagréables, et implique une atteinte injuste à la réputation
de la personne visée par le mal qu'on dit d'elle, la haine, le mépris ou le
ridicule auxquels on l'expose.
[26]

[
52
]

This court has also repeatedly concluded that it
is highly defamatory for an individual of Jewish faith to be compared to or
called a Nazi.
[27]

[
53
]

Finally, in
Couche-Tard inc. c.

Abitbol
,
Justice Claude Dallaire stated :

17. Ces propos et l’annonce de leur publication
imminente justifient l’intervention du Tribunal. Le droit à la réputation est
un droit clair qui ne souffre pas être attaqué injustement. L’ampleur de la
diffusion n’a pas de pertinence pour décider du droit à l’ordonnance
recherchée.
[28]

[
54
]

It’s with all of these elements in mind that the
Court must decide if the prohibitive interlocutory injunction sought against
Mr. Feldman should be granted.

1.3

Discussion

•

Appereance of right

[
55
]

Have Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer demonstrated an
appareance of right to the interloctury injunction sought? More specifically,
have they demonstrated that the Allegations aimed at them are clearly
defamatory?

[
56
]

The Court concludes that they have.

[
57
]

Mr. Feldman’s Allegations are extremely serious
and heavy of consequences for Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer’s reputations.

[
58
]

The Court questions how Mr. Feldman will bring
admissible evidence at trial to prove the truth of his Allegations, but that
remains an issue for the trial judge to decide.

[
59
]

In the interim, the file, as presented, contains
no evidence to support his Allegations.

[
60
]

To the contrary, Mr. Feifer has specifically
denied in his pre-trial examination having inherited 160 million dollars, let
alone half of 4.5 billion dollars.

[
61
]

Mr. Feldman also admits in his Defense that his
Allegations are fictitious.
[29]

[
62
]

Even if the Court were to consider this
admission as being ambiguous given the other allegations in the Defense, it
certainly raises questions as to Mr. Feldman’s credibility, particularly
considering he is a practicing lawyer who litigates from time to time.

[
63
]

As for Mr. Feldman’s intent, there is no
question that his objective is to destroy Irwin. He says as much in the Videos.

[
64
]

The evidence presented is also sufficiently
convincing that his intent towards Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer is one of
punishment for siding with his enemy Irwin.

[
65
]

As such, contrary to Mr. Feldman’s submission,
the Court finds that the Allegations aimed at Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer are
clearly defamatory and reach the high level bar required to allow the issuance
of an interlocutory injunction in similar matters.

•

Serious or irreparable harm

[
66
]

The Court shares the following statements made
by Justice Chantal Masse in
Conseil des juifs
hassidiques du Québec
c
.
Procureur général du Québec
:

Il est de connaissance
judiciaire que la communauté dont il s'agit ici a traversé l'histoire avec une
résilience incomparable, ayant connu des périodes de persécution à différentes
époques, et ayant été victime de l'entreprise d'un génocide lors de la Seconde Guerre
mondiale, la Shoah. Toute cette histoire a laissé des traces et un héritage qui
se sont répercutés et transmis au fil des générations et implique à la fois un
besoin de maintenir des liens communautaires particulièrement forts et un
devoir de mémoire, lequel s'incarne notamment dans le maintien des traditions
de cette communauté et de ses rituels religieux extrêmement exigeants.
[30]

[
67
]

It is difficult to imagine a more detrimental
allegation to the reputation of a member of the Jewish community than being
accused of inheriting and profiting from a fortune criminally obtained from the
victims of the Holocaust.

[
68
]

If the Allegations were to reach Dr. Feifer and
Mr. Feifer’s community, the harm would be extremely serious.

[
69
]

Mr. Feldman argues that since Dr. Feifer and Mr.
Feifer intend to modify their Demand to claim moral and punitive damages, the
harm suffered, if any, is not irreparable.

[
70
]

The Court disagrees.

[
71
]

Firstly, punitive damages are not designed to
compensate. Their purpose is not to repair damages suffered but rather to
sanction and repress illegal conduct.

[
72
]

Secondly, the fact that Dr. Feifer and Mr.
Feifer intend to claim moral damages suffered as a result of Mr. Feldman’s
Allegations does not mean that the damages awarded, if any, can fully repair
the highly negative mark left on their reputation.

[
73
]

In
Hill

v.

Church of
Scientology of Toronto
, Justice Peter C. Cory speaking for the Supreme Court
wrote:

108. Democracy has always
recognized and cherished the fundamental importance of an individual. That
importance must, in turn, be based upon the good repute of a person. It is that
good repute which enhances an individual's sense of worth and value. False allegations
can so very quickly and completely destroy a good reputation.
A reputation
tarnished by libel can seldom regain its former lustre
. A democratic
society, therefore, has an interest in ensuring that its members can enjoy and
protect their good reputation so long as it is merited.
[31]

(The
Court underlines).

[
74
]

Finally, it’s important to stress that Dr. Feifer
and Mr. Feifer have an obligation to minimise their damages.
[32]
Given that the Allegations
have not yet reached their respective communities, the interlocutory injunction
sought will ensure that the harm suffered is not worsened.

•

Balance of inconveniences

[
75
]

Lastly, the circumstances of the present matter
clearly tilt the balance in favor of Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer.

[
76
]

The Court endorses the words of Justice Lucie
Fournier, then sitting on the Superior Court, in
Nadeau

c
.
Dubé
:

45. La balance des inconvénients joue en faveur des
Demandeurs. Ils allèguent subir un grave préjudice des propos du Défendeur,
alors que celui-ci en subirait peu de s’abstenir de tels propos, jusqu’à ce que
jugement intervienne sur l’injonction interlocutoire.
[33]

1.4

Conclusion

[
77
]

For these reasons, the Court finds that Dr. Feifer
and Mr. Feifer have a right to the interlocutory injunction sought.

[
78
]

The Court also finds that in light of Mr.
Feldman’s clear intention to pursue his mission against Dr. Feifer and Mr.
Feifer, the provisional execution notwithstanding appeal must be ordered.
[34]

[
79
]

For the same reasons and in order to ensure that
interlocutory injunction is effective and the Allegations do not otherwise
reach Dr. Feifer and Mr. Feifer’s communities, the Court orders exhibits P-10,
P-15, P-25 and P-27 to be filed under seal, only until the hearing on the
permanent injunction.
[35]

FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT:

[
80
]

GRANTS
in part the

Application for the Issuance of an Interlocutory Injunction
;

[
81
]

ORDERS
the
Defendant Glenn J. Feldman not to publish, disseminate, broadcast or otherwise
communicate, directly or indirectly, either orally or in writing, including
electronically or otherwise the affirmations found in the following paragraphs
of Defendant Glenn J. Feldmand’s Long Form Affidavit signed on March 31, 2020,
namely:

81.1.

Page 16, paragraph 69,

81.2.

Page 19, paragraph 84;

81.3.

Page 21, paragraph 89;

[
82
]

ORDERS
the
Defendant Glenn J. Feldman not to publish, disseminate, broadcast or otherwise
communicate directly or indirectly, either orally or in writing, including
electronically or otherwise, any information, commentary, affirmation or remak
relating to the Estate of the Late Sherry Lande Feifer or the Plaintiffs,
including but not limited to any details on their private life, assets,
properties and financial situation, either personally or in their capacity of
liquidators of the Estate of the Late Sherry Lande Feifer;

[
83
]

ORDERS
the
Defendant Glenn J. Feldman to communicate to the Plaintiffs’ counsel of record
in these proceedings, within fifteen (15) days following the present judgment,
all documents sent and remarks made by the Defendant concerning the Estate of
the Late Sherry Lande Feifer or the Plaintiffs, their assets, properties and
financial situation, whether the Defendant acted directly or indirectly, by any
means, including through the internet, by text message or email or whether
anonymously or not;

[
84
]

ORDERS
that
exhibits P-10, P-15, P-25 and P-27 be filed under seal in the court record and
may not be consulted by anyone, save and except by the parties and their
attorneys;

[
85
]

ORDERS
the
present interlocutory injunction to remain in full force and effect until a
final judgment is issued on the merits;

[
86
]

AUTHORISES
the
Plaintiffs to serve the present judgment to Defendant Glenn J. Feldman by all
means, including by fax and email, at any time outside legal hours, any day of
the week, including a non-judicial day;

[
87
]

DISPENSES
the
Plaintiffs from furnishing security;

[
88
]

ORDERS
the
provisional execution of the present judgment notwithstanding appeal;

[
